location.unitTitle: Secure Data Project and Threat-Model Review

standards: Michigan Computer Science: Data and Analysis
instructions: Create, test, debug, or explain the requested artifact using fictional data and no real credentials or personal information.
Record expected and actual results, include an edge case, and revise after testing.

learnerTasks.prompt: Demonstrate recognising and defending against secure data project and threat-model review independently, with no scaffold, prompts, or worked example in view. Produce a complete correct solution to a new problem, then prove it works: state the expected result first, run or hand-trace at least two cases including one boundary case, and show actual against expected. Then explain the reasoning in your own words well enough that a reader who has not seen recognising and defending against secure data project and threat-model review could follow why each decision was made. Both the working result and the explanation are required — either one alone is incomplete. Anchor today's work inside its unit: this session's evidence is about recognising and defending against secure data project and threat-model review, and it belongs to "Secure Data Project and Threat-Model Review", which also covers separate topics such as requirements and data inventory. Close out with this check before you stop: Identify the item you are least confident about and say what would resolve it. At grade 10 the bar is independent work that justifies its approach against a named alternative you considered and rejected, with the trade-off stated concretely.
Independent complete solution, a two-case verification with expected against actual, and a self-contained written explanation.

learnerSuccessCriteria: The learner completes the central task on secure data project and threat-model review.
The learner supplies evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can name a next step.
accommodations: Access supports may change format, pacing, quantity, setting, or response mode without changing the assessed objective.
